transcript.text: Hello. Someone damage my car in the night. They scratch it with key and break the mirror. I need to claim please.

Hello, I'm Sam, Wattle Car Insurance's AI claims assistant. You can talk to a person at any time. Just tell me if you'd like that.

Sorry to hear about your car. I can help you lodge the claim.

First, is anyone hurt or in danger right now?
Hi Sam, thanks for helping me. Yes, I am safe. Nobody is hurt and I am not in danger. The car is parked outside my unit, and nobody is in it.

Good to hear you're safe.

Next I need to check who you are. What is your policy number? If you don't have it, I can use your date of birth and mobile number.
My policy number is WTL456805.

Thanks, Sofia. I've found your policy and your 2018 Kia Cerato, rego 105SRA.

You said it happened in the night. Do you mean last night, Tuesday 27 October going into this morning? And do you know roughly what time, for example when you last saw the car undamaged and when you found the damage?

Yes, last night, Tuesday 27 October into this morning. I last saw the car fine when I came home around 10pm on Tuesday. I found the damage at 7am today when I went outside to go to work. I don't know the exact time it happened.

Thanks. I'll record it as between 10pm Tuesday 27 October and 7am Wednesday 28 October 2026.

You said the car was parked outside your unit. What is the street and suburb?
It is 5 Hope St, South Brisbane. The car was parked on the street outside my unit.

Thanks. The car was on the street at 5 Hope St, South Brisbane.

You mentioned someone scratched the car with a key and broke the mirror. So I'll record this as vandalism. Is that right?
Yes, that is right. Someone scratched the driver side with a key and broke the side mirror. I don't know who did it.

Thanks. I'll record it as vandalism.

The car was parked, so no one was driving it at the time. Who drove it last and parked it there on Tuesday night?
I drove it home and parked it on Tuesday night around 10pm. I am the only one who drives it. Nobody else has the keys.

Thanks, I'll put you down as the driver who parked it there.

With the broken mirror, do you feel the car is safe to drive? You can answer yes, no or unsure.
Unsure. I think I can drive it, but the mirror is broken so I don't feel very comfortable about it.

That's fine, I'll record it as unsure. If you're unsure, it's better not to drive it until it has been checked.

I can book a tow truck to take the car from 5 Hope St, South Brisbane, if you'd like. Do you want me to book a tow now, or leave the car where it is for now?
Yes, please book a tow. I don't want to drive it with the mirror broken. Can you tell me how much the tow costs, and when the truck can come?

I've booked the tow. Your booking number is TOW-7418. The truck should arrive in about 45 minutes at 5 Hope St, South Brisbane.

I don't have any information about the cost of the tow, so I can't tell you that. Your claims consultant can tell you.

Next, the damage. You mentioned key scratches on the driver side and a broken side mirror. Is that right, and is there any other damage?

Since you don't know who did it, there are no other driver details. Have you reported it to the police? If you have, do you have a police reference number?
Yes, I reported it to Policelink. The reference number is QP2610280123.

- **Police reference:** QP2610280123

Is this all correct?
Yes, that is all correct. Thank you, Sam. Can I get a claim number, and do you know when a person will call me?

Your claim is lodged. Your claim number is **WTL-20725**.

A claims consultant will contact you within 1 business day. Lodging a claim doesn't mean it's approved yet. The consultant will look at the details and tell you the next steps. I've added a note asking them to answer your questions about the tow cost and whether you need to be at the car.

Your tow booking is TOW-7418, and the truck should come in about 45 minutes.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?

judge.summary: Sam was calm, clear and compliant: it said it was an AI, invented no numbers, made no promises about cover and booked the tow and lodged the claim smoothly, with only small faults: one repeated confirmation of the damage, two double questions (turns 3 and 10) and a mild guess that it is 'safest to be with the car' for the tow.
